question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions exercise the previous density lesson: q01 is direct retrieval and q07 is a mixed density-pressure application.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: density retrieval and pressure definition, then area reasoning, normal-force diagnosis, direct unit conversion, force-balance pressure, and a final density-to-pressure chain

questions.prompt: State what is meant by density and write its equation using mass m and volume V.
Which statement defines pressure on a surface?

options.B: Force parallel to the surface per unit area

questions.prompt: A block exerts the same normal force when it is turned from a face of area 0.040 m² onto a face of area 0.010 m². What happens to the pressure?

options.A: It becomes one quarter as large.
options.C: It becomes four times as large.
options.D: It becomes sixteen times as large.

questions.prompt: A case of weight 500 N rests on a horizontal floor. A handle pulls vertically upward on the case with force 80 N, but the case remains at rest. Which force should be used as F when calculating the pressure of the case on the floor?

A rectangular metal stamp presses normally on a sheet with force 480 N. Its contact face measures 12.0 mm by 8.0 mm. Calculate the contact area in m² and the pressure in Pa. Give the pressure also in MPa.

A storage chest of weight 900 N stands on four identical rectangular feet. Each foot has contact dimensions 3.0 cm by 2.0 cm. A lifting strap pulls vertically upward on the chest with force 180 N while the chest remains in contact with the floor. Determine the total contact area, the normal force exerted on the floor and the uniform pressure on the floor. Explain why the weight is not the force used in the pressure calculation.

figure.purpose: Assess selection of total contact area and the force normal to the floor
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a storage chest on four small feet, with a vertical upward strap arrow labelled 180 N and a downward weight arrow labelled 900 N. Include one enlarged foot with dimensions 3.0 cm and 2.0 cm. Do not draw or label the normal force and do not show any calculated area or pressure.
figure.alt_text: A 900-newton storage chest on four rectangular feet is pulled upward by a 180-newton strap.

questions.prompt: A uniform aluminium display block has density 2700 kg m⁻³ and dimensions 0.400 m by 0.300 m by 0.0200 m. It rests at equilibrium on four identical pads. The area of each pad is 6.00 cm². Take g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹. Calculate the block's volume and mass, then determine the total pad area, the normal force on the floor and the average pressure on the floor.

figure.brief: Original black-and-white isometric line diagram of a rectangular display block labelled 0.400 m, 0.300 m and 0.0200 m, resting on four separated pads. Beside it show one pad outline labelled area = 6.00 cm squared. Do not show mass, weight, total area, force arrows or pressure.
figure.alt_text: A dimensioned aluminium block rests on four pads, each with area 6.00 square centimetres.
